normalized.governing_thought: Yes, launch Dispatch Copilot, but in Q4 2027 rather than Q2, and inside a new Pro plan at $91 per seat ($12 above Core) with a pooled usage allowance.
executive_summary: Answer: Yes, launch Dispatch Copilot, but in Q4 2027 rather than Q2, and inside a new Pro plan at $91 per seat ($12 above Core) with a pooled usage allowance. Plan on $1.2–2.9M of new ARR, not $8M. Copilot and the mobile fix are both needed to lift NRR to 105%.
Copilot is worth launching, but the prize is $1.2–2.9M of new ARR, not $8M
Only 14% of beta volunteers paid $149 when asked (17 of 120). The 46% survey figure comes from the 6% of admins who replied, and they run larger accounts
AI can explain at most the 7-point fall in win rate against Routewise: ~110 deals and $0.6M of new ARR a year, not a third of all losses
Package it in Pro at +$12 per seat with 600 requests per seat, not as a $149 add-on
Pro brings in as much ARR ($2.9M at the 33% uptake of the 2023 tier, vs $2.5M for the add-on). Its cost grows with seats, and it matches Routewise's 'AI included in Pro'
With the allowance, company gross margin stays at 75.9% or more in the worst usage case. Bundling Copilot free into Core would cut it to 71.9%
Launch in Q4 2027: fixing the mobile app comes first
Mobile reliability causes 27% of churn and AI features 6%. Two quarters of mobile delay put $0.5M–$1.1M of ARR at risk. Two quarters of Copilot delay put at most $0.6M at risk
Reaching 105% NRR takes both: the mobile fix adds about +1.9 pts and Copilot Pro adds +2.1 to +5.0 pts
Decisions for January: approve the sequence and the Pro design; run a paid early-access test in H1 2027; bring the launch forward to Q2 only if one of the triggers on slide 16 fires.

slides.title: We tested the CPO's plan against five conditions. Demand and timing failed, so the answer changed

claims.claim: Demand: about 46% of accounts will pay $149 a month — Not supported; the add-on is worth $2.5M of ARR at most, not $8.1M
evidence: Paywall test: 17 of 120 beta volunteers (14%) bought
The survey had a 6% response rate, and respondents average 9.4 seats against 6.2 for the base

claims.claim: Economics: the price covers inference and company GM stays ≥75% — Holds, but thin; price per seat and cap usage
evidence: The add-on's own margin is 34% and company GM 76.2%
The top 10% of accounts cost $131 a month to serve against a $149 price

claims.claim: Competition: AI is why we lose to Routewise — Partly; at most $0.6M of new ARR a year is at stake
evidence: Win rate fell 7 points while Routewise was offering 20% off
31% of loss notes 'mention' AI
AI is the main reason for only 6% of churn

claims.claim: Opportunity cost: a two-quarter mobile delay costs less than a two-quarter Copilot delay — Not supported; protect mobile and launch Copilot in Q4 2027
evidence: Mobile drives 27% of churn
A two-quarter delay puts $0.5M–$1.1M of ARR at risk, against ≤$0.6M for Copilot

claims.claim: Proven value: beta gains will hold across the customer base — Unproven; leave retention upside out of the case and test it
evidence: Beta: +11% jobs per dispatcher-hour vs +2% for matched accounts, and 97% vs 93% renewal
But the accounts volunteered and are larger (8.1 seats)

claims.claim: Revised answer: launch in Q4 2027, after the mobile rewrite, inside a per-seat Pro tier with a usage allowance. Size the case at $1.2–2.9M, not $8M.

slides.title: Survey intent overstates demand: what customers actually paid points to at most $2.5M of add-on ARR, not $8M

claims.claim: Few people answered, and they were not typical
evidence: Only 610 of 9,800 admins (6%) replied
They average 9.4 seats against 6.2 for the base

claims.claim: Saying 'likely' is not buying
evidence: When the 120 beta accounts were actually asked to pay $149, 17 did (14%), less than a third of the survey's 46%

claims.claim: 14% is a ceiling, not a base case
evidence: Beta accounts volunteered and are larger (8.1 seats) and more active than the base

claims.claim: Buyers are heavy users
evidence: Those who paid averaged 6,800 requests a month, almost twice the beta mean of 3,600

claims.claim: So what: plan on $1.2–2.5M from a $149 add-on and test conversion on a random sample of accounts that did not volunteer
evidence: Chart, year-1 add-on ARR ($M): Survey 46% 'likely' (CPO) 8.06; Paywall test 14% bought 2.45; Paywall halved for non-volunteers 7% 1.23
Survey: 9,800 × 46% = 4,508 accounts × $1,788 a year = $8.1M
Paywall: 9,800 × 14% = 1,372 accounts × $1,788 a year = $2.5M
Non-volunteer case: 9,800 × 7% = 686 accounts × $1,788 a year = $1.2M
The 7% case is our illustrative haircut for the fact that beta accounts volunteered.

slides.title: Against Routewise, Copilot can win back at most ~110 deals a year (about $0.6M of ARR), not a third of our losses

claims.claim: The VP Sales claim fails a basic check
evidence: Winning back a third of our losses would lift the win rate to 58%, 14 points higher than before Routewise had any AI
VP claim: 1/3 × 983 losses = 328 deals → 58% win rate

claims.claim: Mentioning AI is not the same as losing on AI
evidence: 31% of Q3 loss notes mention AI

claims.claim: Price is a competing explanation
evidence: Routewise offered 20% off the first year in the same quarter it launched AI
price already causes 22% of our churn

claims.claim: So $0.6M a year is the most Copilot can be worth here, and it counts as new-customer growth, not NRR
evidence: Chart, win rate in Routewise deals (%): Q1–Q2 2026 44; Q3 2026 (AI launch + 20% promo) 37; Implied by VP Sales claim 58
2,600 opportunities × 60% = 1,560 Routewise deals a year
7-pt drop × 1,560 = 109 deals × $5,878 = $0.64M of new ARR a year
New account = 6.2 seats × $79 × 12 = $5,878 ARR

claims.claim: A test is available by January. If Q4 2026 win rates stay at or below 37%, AI is the likely cause, and that would make launching sooner more urgent

slides.title: The beta shows Copilot helps engaged accounts, but it cannot yet prove the gains will hold across the customer base

claims.claim: The signal is positive. Productivity rose 9 points more than in matched accounts, and beta accounts renewed more often
evidence: Jobs scheduled per dispatcher-hour: beta +11%, matched +2%, difference +9 pts (trust: Medium)
90-day renewal rate: 97% vs 93%, +4 pts (trust: Low)
Dispatcher hours saved per week: 4.1, no control (trust: Low, self-reported)

claims.claim: Selection bias limits it
evidence: The accounts volunteered and are larger (8.1 vs 6.2 seats) and more active

claims.claim: A few accounts drive the value
evidence: The top 10% of accounts made 58% of all requests
The mean is almost twice the median
Chart, AI requests per account per month: Median 1,900; Mean 3,600; Mean of top 10% 14,500

claims.claim: So what: we leave retention gains out of the business case. Early access for a random sample of Core accounts will measure them on typical customers

slides.title: A Pro tier at +$12 per seat beats both a $149 add-on and a free bundle on margin, cost control and fit against Routewise

claims.claim: A. Paid add-on ($149 per account per month): Reject
evidence: Adoption: 14% ceiling, 7% for non-volunteers
New ARR $2.5M at ceiling, $1.2M at 7%
Cost $1.6M (buyers use 6,800 requests a month)
Feature margin 34%
Company GM 76.2%
NRR uplift +2.1 to +4.3 pts
Fit: Weak: 'AI costs extra'
Cost risk: heavy users cost nearly the full price to serve

claims.claim: B. Pro tier (+$12 per seat per month, 600 pooled requests per seat): Recommend
evidence: Adoption: 33% (2023 higher-tier precedent) base, 14% low
New ARR $2.9M base, $1.2M low
Cost $1.6M base, at most $1.9M under the allowance
Feature margin 46% base, at least 34% under the allowance
Company GM 76.5% base, at least 75.9%
NRR uplift +2.1 to +5.0 pts
Fit: Parity: 'AI included in Pro'
Revenue grows with seats and the allowance limits cost

claims.claim: C. Include in Core at no charge: Reject: breaches the 75% margin floor
evidence: New ARR $0
Cost $3.5M with no revenue to cover it
Feature margin negative
Company GM 71.9%, below the floor
Cost has no ceiling

slides.title: A flat $149 price attracts heavy users: serving the top 10% of accounts would use up 88% of the price in inference alone

claims.claim: A flat price selects for heavy use
evidence: The accounts that paid used almost twice the beta mean
Chart, inference cost per account per month ($): Median 17.1; Mean 32.4; Paywall buyers 61.2; Top 10% 130.5; Add-on price 149
Break-even: $149 ÷ $0.009 = 16,556 requests a month

claims.claim: Pricing per seat follows usage
evidence: $4.00 of inference per seat against a $12 price leaves 67% before platform cost
3,600 requests ÷ 8.1 beta seats = 444 requests per seat

claims.claim: Smaller accounts pay less
evidence: A typical 6.2-seat account pays $74 a month for Pro instead of $149
price causes 22% of churn

claims.claim: So what: charge per seat and set an allowance, so that one heavy account cannot turn the feature unprofitable

slides.title: A pooled allowance of 600 requests per seat keeps company gross margin above 75% even if only heavy users upgrade

claims.claim: Without an allowance, Pro could breach the floor
evidence: If upgraders behave like the paywall buyers, company GM falls to 74.1%
Inference: 3,234 accounts × 6,800 requests × $0.009 × 12 = $2.4M; plus $0.6M platform = $3.0M extra cost against $2.9M of Pro ARR

claims.claim: 600 requests per seat caps the downside
evidence: $5.40 of inference against $12, so company GM stays at 75.9% or more
Chart, GM vs 75% floor (pts): Today 3; Pro at beta average 1.47; Pro stress with allowance 0.91; Pro stress no allowance -0.87; Copilot free in Core -3.10

claims.claim: Typical users never hit it
evidence: The beta average is 444 requests per seat, and the median account used about 235 per seat

claims.claim: Margin improves after 2027
evidence: Our $0.009 rate is fixed through December 2027, and the provider's list prices fell 35% last year

slides.title: The recommended package adds Copilot to a new Pro plan at $91 per seat and leaves the $79 Core plan unchanged

claims.claim: Price: $91 per seat per month (Core $79 + $12); Core keeps its price so no one is forced to upgrade
evidence: price causes 22% of churn
Typical account: 6.2 seats × $12 = $74 a month extra

claims.claim: Included: all three Copilot features, positioned as 'AI included in Pro', the same as Routewise
evidence: schedule proposals, quote drafts from technician notes, call summaries

claims.claim: Usage guardrail: 600 AI requests per seat per month, pooled across the account
evidence: 1.35× the beta average
Top-up packs at $20 per 1,000 requests (55% margin at $0.009)

claims.claim: Migration: the 17 accounts paying $149 move to Pro; other beta accounts are offered early access at the Pro price
Value check: Pro pays for itself many times over at the hours the beta reported
evidence: Beta dispatchers reported saving 4.1 hours a week, about 17.8 hours a month per account
A 6.2-seat account pays $74 a month, so it breaks even at $4.20 per hour saved
Even if the real saving is a quarter of what was reported, the break-even is about $17 per hour
The $149 add-on would need $8.40 per hour at the reported saving

slides.title: Customers' biggest problem is the mobile app, not AI: it causes 4.5× as much churn and gets twice as many first-choice votes

claims.claim: the mobile app is where churn is lost, and churn is where NRR is lost
evidence: Chart, main churn reason 2026 (%): Mobile app reliability 27; Price 22; Missing integrations 15; Out of business/sold 14; Switched for AI features 6; Other 16
Chart, feature ranked first (%): Reliable technician mobile app 38; AI scheduling 19
All reasons (14%): 1,372 accounts, $8.1M ARR lost
Mobile app reliability (27%): 370 accounts, $2.2M
Switched for AI features (6%): 82 accounts, $0.5M

claims.claim: Mobile-driven churn costs about $2.2M of ARR a year, 4.5 times the $0.5M lost to AI features. That is why the Head of Customer Success is right to guard the rewrite.

slides.title: A two-quarter delay to the mobile rewrite puts up to twice as much ARR at risk as a two-quarter delay to Copilot

claims.claim: Losses to churn are permanent
evidence: Chart, ARR lost in two-quarter delay ($M): Delay mobile, fixes all 1.09; fixes half 0.54; Delay Copilot full credit 0.56; half credit 0.28
Copilot: ($0.64M win-rate gap + $0.48M AI churn) × 0.5 yr = $0.56M; half credit = $0.28M

claims.claim: Copilot revenue is mostly postponed, not lost
evidence: Six months of deferral costs $0.1M–$0.7M of gross profit

claims.claim: The threshold is not demanding. The rewrite only has to fix 26–52% of the churn caused by the app's reliability
evidence: mobile-first wins if the rewrite fixes more than 52% (full credit) or 26% (half credit) of mobile churn

claims.claim: The engineering cost is the same in either order
evidence: 14 × $210k × 0.5 yr = $1.47M in either order

claims.claim: So what: do the mobile rewrite first, unless the January data shows AI is costing us deals (slide 16)

slides.title: Hitting 105% NRR by 2028 is safest with both levers: Copilot alone needs 26% of accounts on Pro, but with the mobile fix 14% is enough

claims.claim: Both levers reach the 105% target
evidence: Mobile fix (halves mobile churn): +1.9 pts low and base
Copilot Pro (14% / 33% adoption): +2.1 pts / +5.0 pts
Chart: NRR today 101; mobile fix +1.89; Copilot Pro at 14% +2.13; 2028 NRR 105.0
1 NRR point = $0.58M of ARR

claims.claim: Copilot alone would need 26% of accounts on Pro to close the 4-point gap ($2.3M)
With the mobile fix, Copilot needs only 14% adoption, the same rate we saw in the paywall test
Mobile alone would have to remove all of the churn it causes (+3.8 pts) to come close
So what: the sequence matters less than delivering both by 2028

slides.title: The roadmap keeps mobile on track in H1, uses that time to test Pro pricing, and launches Copilot in Q4 2027

claims.claim: Mobile app rewrite with full team, no diversion in H1 2027; Copilot early access for 240 beta + ~250 random Core accounts at the Pro price; Copilot launch build (14 engineers); Pro tier on sale / general availability; ramp toward 14–33% adoption
evidence: Early-access inference ≈ 490 accounts × 3,600 req × $0.009 × 12 ≈ $0.19M a year

claims.claim: Each gate can bring the launch forward or change the price
evidence: Gate 1 · Jan 2027: Read Q4 2026 win rate vs Routewise (after the promo)
Gate 2 · end Q2 2027: Early-access adoption and requests per seat confirm the $12 price and the 600 allowance
2028: NRR target of 105%. Re-price on new inference terms
Inference contract: Renegotiate (fixed to Dec 2027)

slides.title: Waiting carries risks, but each one can be watched and has a specific mitigation

claims.claim: Routewise pulls further ahead in 2027
evidence: Up to $0.6M of new ARR a year if AI is what is driving the win-rate drop
Mitigation: 'AI included in Pro, early access now'; Gate 1 brings launch forward

claims.claim: Pro adoption comes in below 14%
evidence: NRR falls short of 105%, and the feature only covers its platform cost
Mitigation: early access on random Core sample; adjust at Gate 2

claims.claim: Heavy usage erodes margin
evidence: Without a cap, company GM could fall to 74.1%
Mitigation: 600-request pooled allowance, top-up packs, usage meter

claims.claim: Productivity gains do not hold for typical accounts
evidence: Mitigation: measure on non-volunteers; retention upside already left out

claims.claim: The mobile rewrite under-delivers or slips
evidence: The main reason for choosing this order disappears

claims.claim: Inference prices change after 2027

slides.title: Five assumptions carry the recommendation, and each comes with a test and a trigger that would change the plan

claims.claim: The win-rate drop is partly Routewise's price promo, not only AI
evidence: The 20% promo ran in the same quarter (Q3 2026)
Trigger: Stays ≤37% → bring Copilot forward to Q2 2027 (Pro design unchanged)

claims.claim: The rewrite removes at least 26–52% of mobile-driven churn
evidence: Mobile causes 27% of churn and is the top request for 38%
Trigger: Below 26% → launch Copilot first

claims.claim: Doing mobile first moves Copilot back only two quarters
evidence: Inferred from the staffing note (14 of 60 engineers)
Trigger: If 14 engineers can come from outside mobile → launch in Q2 with no trade-off. If Copilot would slip past Q1 2028 → revisit

claims.claim: 14–33% of accounts take Pro
evidence: 2023 tier precedent: 33%. Paywall test: 14%
Trigger: Below 14% → rethink the price before general availability

claims.claim: Usage averages about 444 requests per seat
evidence: Beta mean, from volunteers with concentrated usage
Trigger: Above 600 → lower the allowance or raise the price

normalized.recommendation: Launch Dispatch Copilot in Q4 2027, after the mobile rewrite, inside a new Pro plan at $91 per seat ($12 above Core) that includes Copilot with 600 pooled requests per seat; Core stays at $79; retire the $149 add-on. Keep the mobile rewrite fully staffed in H1 2027, run a paid early-access test in H1 2027, reset the Copilot business case to $1.2–2.9M of ARR, set the NRR plan as the mobile fix plus Pro adoption of at least 14%, and bring the launch forward to Q2 only if one of the triggers on slide 16 fires.

alternatives_considered.option: CPO plan: launch in Q2 2027 as a paid add-on at $149 per account per month (~$8M ARR in year 1)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected. Demand and timing conditions 'Not supported'; add-on worth $2.5M of ARR at most; heavy users cost nearly the full price to serve; weak fit against Routewise ('AI costs extra').

alternatives_considered.option: B. Pro tier: +$12 per seat per month with 600 pooled requests per seat
alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommend. $2.9M base / $1.2M low ARR, company GM 76.5% base and at least 75.9%; parity with Routewise 'AI included in Pro'.

alternatives_considered.option: C. Include Copilot in Core at no charge
alternatives_considered.treatment: Reject: breaches the 75% margin floor (company GM 71.9%); $3.5M cost with no revenue; cost has no ceiling.

alternatives_considered.option: Launch Copilot first / delay the mobile rewrite by two quarters
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: a two-quarter mobile delay puts $0.5M–$1.1M of ARR at risk vs ≤$0.6M for Copilot; launch Copilot first only if the rewrite would remove below 26% of mobile churn.
Only if a trigger fires: Q4 2026 Routewise win rate stays ≤37%, or the 14 engineers can come from outside mobile.

alternatives_considered.option: Copilot alone or mobile alone to reach 105% NRR
alternatives_considered.treatment: Copilot alone would need 26% Pro adoption; mobile alone would have to remove all mobile churn (+3.8 pts) to come close; both levers recommended.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: All company, competitor and market figures are synthetic benchmark data; prepared using only the internal briefing pack.
14% paywall conversion is a ceiling because beta accounts volunteered and are larger; 7% non-volunteer case is an illustrative haircut.
Pre-AI win rate assumed to be the Q1–Q2 2026 rate; the win-rate drop is partly Routewise's 20% price promo.
Beta gains are unproven across the base due to selection bias; retention upside left out of the business case; hours saved are self-reported.
Inference $0.009 per request fixed through Dec 2027; platform $0.6M a year counted as cost of revenue (if opex, feature margins rise by about 20 pts).
Pro usage = beta mean 444 requests per seat per month; Pro adoption 33% base (2023 precedent), 14% low (paywall).
Churned accounts assumed average size (6.2 seats); if smaller, mobile ARR at risk is overstated.
Mobile rewrite effect is illustrative (50% and 100% of mobile churn); break-even 26–52% is the number to challenge.
Doing mobile first moves Copilot back exactly two quarters (inferred; CTO to confirm the 14 engineers are free in Q3 2027).
Allowance (600 requests) and top-up price ($20 per 1,000) are proposals to test in early access and tune at Gate 2.
Risks: Routewise pulls ahead; Pro adoption below 14%; heavy usage erodes margin; productivity gains don't hold; mobile rewrite under-delivers or slips; inference prices change after 2027.
Judgement calls made without the chance to consult the executive team; owners are suggestions for the CEO to confirm.
next_steps: Decision: Sequence. Keep the mobile rewrite fully staffed in H1 2027 and launch Copilot in Q4 2027, unless a trigger on slide 16 fires
Decision: Packaging and price. Approve a Pro plan at $91 per seat that includes Copilot with 600 pooled requests per seat. Core stays at $79. Retire the $149 add-on
Decision: Targets. Reset the Copilot business case to $1.2–2.9M of ARR. Set the NRR plan as the mobile fix plus Pro adoption of at least 14%
Pull Q4 2026 win rates in Routewise deals and read Gate 1 — VP Sales — Jan 2027
Confirm the 14 engineers can start Copilot in Q3 2027, or come from outside mobile — CTO — Jan 2027
Estimate how much mobile-driven churn the rewrite removes — Head of CS + CPO — Feb 2027
Launch paid early access: beta accounts plus ~250 randomly chosen Core accounts — CPO — Mar 2027
Gate 2 (end Q2 2027): early-access adoption and requests per seat confirm the $12 price and the 600 allowance
